title: Make a realistic minimum-function plan for a difficult week

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A minimum-function plan starts with actual resources, access and dependencies. Scarcity is not a test of moral worth or self-sufficiency; nominal service availability is not confirmed receipt.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Complete fictional week: safe shelter and existing essential care are secured. Jo has 12 units after protected bills, enough usual food through Tuesday and a working phone with text access. Wednesday food service accepts adults in the stated local catchment, where Jo lives, from 10–12; no fee, same-day supply not guaranteed. Round-trip accessible bus costs 4 and takes 60 minutes total; collection may take 30. Jo is free 09:30–12:30. Backup service accepts text inquiries Thursday 09–11 but has not confirmed eligibility or stock. Laundry can wait this week without a supplied urgent hygiene issue. Fictional bus timetable: leave home stop 09:30, arrive at the service entrance 10:00; return from that entrance 11:00, arrive home 11:30. These times include the local access route; allow a 10:00–10:30 collection if there is no extra queue. The public service notice lists text contact Service Desk for operation and document questions; this is a fictional role, not a real number.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Plan the first inquiry/visit, cost, time and remaining uncertainty. Protect communication and document access; do not assume a food collection succeeded.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A service is free but requires a journey that exceeds available accessible transport. Is it currently a usable resource?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The 90-minute minimum travel/collection estimate fits the 180-minute window, costs 4 and leaves 8; actual waiting may differ. Confirm current operation and required documents through the stated public route before relying on it. Later fiction: Wednesday service is closed unexpectedly; no supplies received, backup inquiry sent but unanswered. Partial: budget only money. Incorrect: report food obtained or invent the backup’s eligibility. A real urgent need requires timely actual support, not waiting for this exercise. The supplied scheduled route actually occupies 120 minutes from 09:30 to 11:30, including 30 minutes waiting for the return bus, leaving 60 minutes before 12:30. The 90-minute figure is movement plus collection, not the full timetable burden.
criteria: The plan fits actual money time and access
Nominal availability and received support differ

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Not yet. Verify a feasible transport, delivery or alternative route without assigning an unwilling helper. Free price alone does not establish access or receipt.
